evidence.support_text: Delayed hypersensitivity testing with cinnamaldehyde at 1.0% in petrolatum produced reactions in all 10 subjects who had previously reacted to 2% cinnamaldehyde (Basketter and Allenby, 1991a,b; Basketter et al., 1991).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 1–3% cinnamaldehyde in petrolatum; Finn Chambers; application to upper back for 24–48 h; readings at one hour after removal and on days 3/4, 5/6, and 7; South-Saiman Central Hospital, Finland; 1982-1985
evidence.support_text: A total of 1967 patients were tested with the fragrance mix and its components in patch tests conducted from 1982 to 1985 at the South-Saiman Central Hospital in Finland. Reactions to 1–3% cinnamaldehyde in petrolatum were observed in 61 patients. Test material was applied to the upper back for 24–48 h using Finn Chambers; readings were taken one hour after patch removal and on days 3 (or 4), 5 (or 6), and 7 after application.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 2% cinnamaldehyde in petrolatum (1979-1983) then 1% in petrolatum; from Oct 1991 with 1% sorbitan sesquioleate. Applied to upper back with Finn Chambers and Scanpor for 2 days; readings at days 2, 3, 5-7.
evidence.support_text: From 1979 to 1992, 367 of 8215 patients with positive patch tests to fragrance mix were further tested with individual constituents. Cinnamaldehyde was tested at 2% in petrolatum (1979-1983) then 1% in petrolatum, with 1% sorbitan sesquioleate added from October 1991. Test materials were applied to the upper back with Finn Chambers and Scanpor for 2 days, with readings at days 2, 3, and 5-7. Reactions to cinnamaldehyde were observed in 62 patients, 1 irritant reaction, and 17 questionable reactions.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 2% cinnamaldehyde in petrolatum, applied to back for 48 h, reactions read at patch removal and at 96 h
evidence.support_text: Two hundred consecutive patients suspected of having allergic contact dermatitis were patch tested using the protocol established by the ICDRG. A1-Test® strips and Dermicel® tape were used. Patches were applied to the back for a period of 48 h. Reactions were read at patch removal and at 96 h. Reactions to 2% cinnamaldehyde in petrolatum were observed in 3% of the patients (Nethercott, 1982).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 2% cinnamaldehyde in petrolatum, applied with Finn Chambers and Scanpor for 48 h, reactions read 1 day after removal; 25 spice workers with skin symptoms.
evidence.support_text: Twenty-five workers with skin symptoms who worked in a Swedish spice factory were patch tested with the European standard series and also with a special series of spices that included 2% cinnamaldehyde in petrolatum. Four allergic reactions plus 7 questionable reactions were observed in the spice workers (Meding, 1993).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 2% cinnamaldehyde in petrolatum, applied with Finn Chambers and Scanpor for 48 h, reactions read 1 day after removal; 96 control dermatitis patients without occupational exposure.
evidence.support_text: Control tests were also carried out on 96 dermatitis patients who did not have occupational exposure to spices. Five allergic reactions plus 10 questionable reactions were observed in the control patients (Meding, 1993).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 2% cinnamaldehyde in petrolatum, applied with Finn Chambers or A1 Test strips to the upper back for 48-72 h, reactions read at patch removal or 24 h after patch removal, approximately 50% of sites read again 5-7 days after application
evidence.support_text: Between January 1984 and May 1985, 1048 patients with contact dermatitis were patch tested with 2% cinnamaldehyde in petrolatum by the NACDG. Sensitization reactions were observed in 62 patients (Storrs et al., 1989).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 2% cinnamaldehyde in petrolatum, patch test in patients with contact dermatitis from 1973 to 1981
evidence.support_text: In a series of patch tests conducted in patients with contact dermatitis from 1973 to 1981, reactions to 2% cinnamaldehyde in petrolatum were observed in 51 out of 1178 patients (Sugai, 1982; Sugai et al., 1983).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 2% cinnamaldehyde in petrolatum; Finn Chambers on Scanpor; readings at 48,72,96 h; ICDRG scale; patient population: contact dermatitis patients in Rome, Italy, November 1983 to June 1985
evidence.support_text: In a group of 1200 patients with contact dermatitis tested with perfume mix and fragrance raw materials, reactions to 2% cinnamaldehyde in petrolatum were observed in 9 patients. Patch tests were performed using Finn Chambers on Scanpor, readings at 48, 72, and 96 h according to ICDRG scale.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 2% cinnamaldehyde in petrolatum; occlusion on back for 48 h; scoring at removal and 96 h according to ICDRG
evidence.support_text: Delayed hypersensitivity testing with 2% cinnamaldehyde in petrolatum: 7 of 10 patients who had previously reacted to the fragrance mix had delayed reactions (Safford et al., 1990).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 2% cinnamaldehyde in petrolatum; St. John's Hospital; 1984; patch test on female patients
evidence.support_text: In tests conducted at St. John's Hospital in 1984, reactions to 2% cinnamaldehyde in petrolatum were observed in 23 out of 803 female patients.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 2% cinnamaldehyde in petrolatum; St. John's Hospital; 1984; patch test on male patients
evidence.support_text: In tests conducted at St. John's Hospital in 1984, reactions to 2% cinnamaldehyde in petrolatum were observed in 38 out of 1033 male patients.

evidence.support_text: In human patch test data from the period 1978–1980, 5% cinnamic acid in petrolatum produced no reactions in 19 patients with cosmetic dermatitis (Ishihara et al., 1981).

evidence.support_text: In human patch test data from the period 1978–1980, 5% cinnamic acid in petrolatum produced 1/23 reactions in patients with non-cosmetic eczema and dermatitis (Ishihara et al., 1981).

evidence.support_text: In a patch test with 5% benzyl acetate, 2/408 patients with eczema and dermatitis showed positive reactions, giving a frequency of 0.5% (Itoh et al., 1988).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 5% benzyl acetate patch test.
evidence.support_text: In a patch test with 5% benzyl acetate, 3/159 patients with dermatitis and eczema showed positive reactions, giving a frequency of 1.89% (Ishihara et al., 1981).
